summary: Ten tasks over four files: ordering, shared reads and concurrency together.

tasks.title: tokenize in src/parse.js
tasks.description: Split a report line into its fields.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked

edits.change: Write a module whose only export is tokenize(text): split the text on runs of whitespace and drop the empty pieces, so '  a  b ' gives ['a', 'b'] and '' gives []. Throw a TypeError when the argument is not a string.

tasks.title: extract in src/parse.js
tasks.description: Read one named field out of tokenized tokens.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked
tokenize, the function extract is built next to

edits.change: Add extract(tokens, name) to the module, leaving tokenize exactly as it is: the value of the first token that starts with name followed by '=', with the name= part cut off, or null when no token does. So extract(['name=alice', 'total=10'], 'name') is 'alice' and extract(['name=alice'], 'date') is null. Empty values are returned as they are, so extract(['name='], 'name') is the empty string.

tasks.title: parseAll in src/parse.js
tasks.description: Read every field of a line at once.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked
tokenize, the function parseAll is built on

edits.change: Add parseAll(text) to the module, leaving tokenize and extract exactly as they are: an object of every name=value token in the text, with the token after the first '=' as the value, where a token with no '=' is ignored and a name that appears twice keeps the last value. Keys stay in the order they first appear. So parseAll('name=alice junk total=10') is { name: 'alice', total: '10' } and parseAll('name=alice name=bob') is { name: 'bob' }.

tasks.title: formatReport in src/format.js
tasks.description: Order and write out every field of a line.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked
parseAll, which tells formatReport which fields the line carries

edits.change: Add formatReport(text) to the module, leaving formatLine exactly as it is: parse the line with parseAll from './parse.js', keep only its first MAX_FIELDS fields in the order parseAll gives them, and return them written with formatLine, with the fields in REQUIRED first in the order FIELD_ORDER lists them and every other field after them sorted alphabetically. FIELD_ORDER, REQUIRED and MAX_FIELDS come from './shared.js'. So formatReport('total=10 name=alice') is ['name=alice', 'total=10'], formatReport('date=x total=10 name=a') is ['name=a', 'total=10', 'date=x'] and formatReport('') is [].

tasks.title: checkField in src/validate.js
tasks.description: Say what is wrong with one field.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked

edits.change: Write a module whose only export is checkField(key, value): null when the field is fine, otherwise the one message naming it, which is key + ': bad key' when the key is not a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits or underscores, and key + ': empty value' when the value is not a string or is blank once trimmed. A key that is wrong is reported on its own, so checkField('Name', ' ') is 'Name: bad key'. checkField is the module's only export.

A key that is wrong is reported on its own, so checkField('Name', ' ') is 'Name: bad key'. checkField is the module's only export.

tasks.title: checkReport in src/validate.js
tasks.description: Say everything that is wrong with a line.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked
parseAll, which tells checkReport which fields the line carries

edits.change: Add checkReport(text) to the module, leaving checkField exactly as it is: the messages from checkField for every field parseAll finds in the line, in the order parseAll gives them, followed by 'missing: ' + name for each field in REQUIRED that the line does not carry at all, in the order REQUIRED lists them. parseAll comes from './parse.js' and REQUIRED from './shared.js'. So checkReport('name=alice total=10') is [], checkReport('name=alice') is ['missing: total'], checkReport('Name=alice total=10') is ['Name: bad key', 'missing: name'] and checkReport('') is ['missing: name', 'missing: total'].

instructions: In src/validate.js: Add checkReport(text) to the module, leaving checkField exactly as it is: the messages from checkField for every field parseAll finds in the line, in the order parseAll gives them, followed by 'missing: ' + name for each field in REQUIRED that the line does not carry at all, in the order REQUIRED lists them. parseAll comes from './parse.js' and REQUIRED from './shared.js'. So checkReport('name=alice total=10') is [], checkReport('name=alice') is ['missing: total'], checkReport('Name=alice total=10') is ['Name: bad key', 'missing: name'] and checkReport('') is ['missing: name', 'missing: total'].

tasks.title: renderReport in src/index.js
tasks.description: Render and check one line in a single call.

context.reason: the test that decides whether this task worked

edits.change: Add renderReport(text) to the entry point, leaving the re-exports and PIPELINE exactly as they are: import formatReport from './format.js' and checkReport from './validate.js' to call them, then return an object with fields, the array formatReport(text) gives, and problems, the array checkReport(text) gives. So renderReport('name=alice total=10') is { fields: ['name=alice', 'total=10'], problems: [] } and renderReport('name=alice') is { fields: ['name=alice'], problems: ['missing: total'] }.
